name: Brown-fat cooling patch
subtitle: a patch that chills skin to burn fat

effects.effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
adrenaline sets the body to fight or flight

effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
how: Cold makes the body burn its brown fat, the tissue that exists to make heat, which is why a chilly room beats a warm one for weight, but nobody keeps up with cold baths. A thin film that cools whenever a voltage is applied, worn over the brown fat at the collarbone, chills just that patch of skin in short bursts, which releases the fight-or-flight signal that switches the tissue on, without making the wearer cold.
obstacle: Adult brown fat burns only a few hundred extra calories a day at best, and it gets used to the cold within weeks.
why: Solid-state cooling makes targeted cold therapy wearable instead of a cold bath.
real: Local cooling of supraclavicular brown fat by gel-pack patch, Peltier element or phase-change vest is patented and sold commercially, and a stretchable thermoelectric skin patch holding skin at 32 C was demonstrated (Science Advances, 2019), but no electrocaloric wearable exists and none of the solid-state devices has been shown to activate brown fat.
